opener: Father, I'm tired of needing a round of applause before I believe I did something right.
paragraphs: You know the real exhaustion isn't the work — it's the waiting to find out if the work counted, if anyone noticed, if the hours nobody saw were actually worth it. I have smiled through being overlooked and called it humility when it was really just exhaustion wearing a nicer outfit. I keep performing for rooms that forget me the moment I leave them, and somewhere in all that performing, I lost the sound of Your voice underneath everyone else's silence.

So tonight I'm done auditioning for people who were never assigned to approve me. Let me hear You say it's enough before I need one more voice to confirm it — You already clapped over me before I did anything worth clapping for. Strengthen these tired hands the way You promised, uphold me with Your own right hand, and give me the courage to keep laboring quietly, faithfully, for an audience of One. In Jesus' name, amen.
bold: You already clapped over me before I did anything worth clapping for
kicker: A Prayer For When Nobody's Clapping
footerNote: Save this for the morning you need reminding who's actually watching
